newsitem.title: EGYPT: Almost 1,000 Cairo students protest against Israel.
newsitem.headline: Almost 1,000 Cairo students protest against Israel.

text.p: Almost 1,000 Egyptian students stormed out of Cairo University on Tuesday and briefly marched outside campus to protest Israeli policies in the Middle East.
The students burned two Israeli flags and chanted anti-Israeli slogans before riot police officers securing the area around the university, located in the suburb of Giza, shepherded them back inside.
Some of the students were clutching a gold-painted model of Islam's third holiest shrine, the Al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem, and chanted "We will give up our life and our blood for Jerusalem."

The protest was the latest in a series staged by students on Cairo campuses against Israel's controversial decision to build housing for Jews in Arab East Jerusalem, which the Palestinians claim as a capital for their future state.
On Monday, thousands of students protests at Ain Shams University and others also demonstrated in the Azhar Islamic university and Helwan University.

In 1994, riot police fired volley of tear gas to disperse hundreds of university students who poured out of their campuses to protest the killing of scores of Palestinians by a Jewish militant in the West Bank town of Hebron.
